entry.title: Abyssos: Technical Analysis of a New Modular RAT
entry.content:
red-team · c2

Abyssos is a modular remote access trojan (RAT) written in C++ targeting Windows systems with capabilities including credential theft, file exfiltration, VNC-based remote access, keylogging, and UAC bypass. The malware uses LLVM-based obfuscation (control flow flattening, string encryption), AES-GCM encryption for C2 communication, and employs anti-analysis techniques including hypervisor detection and process name checking. While currently in active development with limited observed deployment, Abyssos represents a significant threat due to its modular architecture enabling ongoing capability expansion and evasion techniques. Organizations should implement endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools with behavioral analysis capabilities, monitor for suspicious VNC and remote shell sessions, block identified C2 IP addresses (213.145.86.42, 209.99.184.223), and maintain updated antivirus/anti-malware solutions with Zscaler's threat definitions (Win64.PWS.Abyssos).

Applications using user-controlled input in where() statements before calling deleteBatch() are vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. There is no indication this is currently exploited in the wild. Affected applications should immediately upgrade to a patched version and audit any deleteBatch() calls preceded by where() conditions for potential exploitation.

entry.title: CodeIgniter: Uploaded file extension validation bypass in `is_image` and `mime_in` rules (CVE-2026-63223)
entry.content:
vulnerability · file-upload-bypass · CVE-2026-63223

CodeIgniter 4 framework (before v4.7.4) contains an unsafe file upload validation bypass in the `is_image` and `mime_in` validation rules that allows attackers to upload executable files with image MIME types, leading to remote code execution when files are saved with client-supplied names in web-accessible directories. This is critical severity and likely exploited in the wild given the common misconfiguration patterns involved. Immediately upgrade to v4.7.4 or later; as a workaround, implement independent safe extension validation using `ext_in` rule, avoid using client-supplied filenames, and store uploads outside web-accessible directories.

entry.title: crypto-js: Insufficient Entropy in Cryptographic Secret Generation via Vulnerable CryptoJS Dependency Chain (CVE-2026-71851)
entry.content:
vulnerability · insufficient-entropy · CVE-2026-71851

CryptoJS library versions containing `WordArray.random()` suffer from insufficient entropy in cryptographic secret generation, producing only ~2^39 bits of effective entropy for 128-bit requests and ~2^47 for 256-bit requests instead of the full keyspace. This vulnerability is critical as it allows attackers to enumerate possible cryptographic secrets on commodity hardware, and is exploited in the wild with downstream wallet applications using the function for BIP39 recovery phrase generation. Immediate action required: update CryptoJS to a patched version and audit any applications using this library for key generation, particularly cryptocurrency wallets and sensitive credential systems, regenerating compromised secrets.

entry.content:

This technique exploits legitimate system automation features to establish persistence and external connectivity without requiring traditional malware signatures, making detection difficult for endpoint tools. The severity is high due to potential for unauthorized system access and lateral movement, though exploitation in the wild remains tied to targeted operations rather than mass campaigns. Organizations should implement strict LaunchAgent monitoring, restrict outbound tunnel creation, enforce network segmentation for admin applications, and treat suspicious reverse tunnel activity as security incidents regardless of whether it appears to be "vibe-coded" rather than confirmed malicious.

entry.title: Craft CMS: Passkey login accepts replayed WebAuthn assertions
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

Craft CMS 5.10.3 and earlier versions contain a critical vulnerability in passkey/WebAuthn login that accepts user-supplied `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` and fails to update stored credential counters, allowing captured login requests to be replayed indefinitely. An unauthenticated attacker who obtains a single passkey assertion can authenticate as the victim by replaying the captured request, bypassing WebAuthn's replay protection mechanism. This vulnerability is likely exploitable in the wild given its straightforward nature. Immediately upgrade to a patched version and audit login logs for suspicious WebAuthn activity; consider temporarily disabling passkey authentication until patching is completed.

entry.title: Traefik: Authentication Bypass via Path Traversal in ReplacePathRegex Middleware (CVE-2026-65600)
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass · CVE-2026-65600

Traefik's ReplacePathRegex middleware contains a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-65600) where improperly configured regex replacements allow path traversal attacks to bypass security controls. Crafted requests can generate unnormalized paths like `/../admin` that forward to backends without validation, potentially exposing protected resources when the backend normalizes the path. This affects Traefik v2 and v3. Users must update to patched versions and review ReplacePathRegex configurations to ensure regex patterns include mandatory separators between captured segments; consider alternative middleware if traversal patterns are unavoidable.

The attack has been demonstrated to leak sensitive data including Linux password hashes from affected systems. Severity is high as it defeats current protections, though wild exploitation likelihood is currently unknown given the technical sophistication required. Mitigation requires updated CPU microcode and kernel patches; users should monitor vendor advisories from Intel, AMD, and Linux distributions for available fixes and apply them promptly.

entry.title: Borrowing Windows Hello keys for authentication and persistence
entry.content:
red-team · auth-bypass

Windows Hello for Business (WHFB) key material can be extracted from an authenticated user session and leveraged for single sign-on and device registration without requiring PIN verification or user presence validation, enabling authentication and persistence attacks against Entra ID. This technique exploits inherent WHFB design rather than a specific vulnerability, allowing attackers with session access to obtain Primary Refresh Tokens and register new devices using stolen cryptographic keys. No patch is available as Microsoft considers this a design consequence of WHFB architecture; mitigation requires enforcing strict session isolation, privileged access workstation (PAW) policies, and monitoring for unusual Entra ID authentication patterns and device registrations.

entry.title: Trojanized npm Packages Employ NullReceiver Tactic to Decode C2 IP from Blockchain
entry.content:
red-team · c2

Two trojanized npm packages (bianira-ui and fluid-type-ui) employ the NullReceiver technique to decode C2 infrastructure from Ethereum blockchain transactions, evolving the EtherHiding C2 obfuscation method. This supply chain attack leverages null-value Ethereum transfers to conceal command server IP addresses, making detection more difficult than traditional DNS/IP-based C2 callbacks. Severity is high given the npm ecosystem's broad reach; exploitation in the wild has been confirmed with these packages. Immediate action: remove affected packages from environments, audit npm dependencies for similar patterns, implement software composition analysis tooling, and monitor for artifacts indicating NullReceiver C2 communication (blockchain transaction analysis or network egress to Ethereum RPC endpoints).

There is no indication of active exploitation in the wild, but the ease of exploitation is high. Immediate patching is essential; update Flowise to a patched version that implements proper authentication on this endpoint and avoids returning tokens in response bodies, or implement strict network-level access controls as a temporary mitigation.

This vulnerability is critical in severity and the recommended action is to immediately patch to a patched version once available, and restrict administrative access to Flowise instances in the interim.

The technique exploits the flexibility of capability output formats (PIC/PICO/COFF) that require in-memory runners, making detection difficult since the malicious payload executes entirely in memory without touching disk. Severity is moderate-to-high as this is an active evasion technique observed in red team operations and likely exploited by advanced threat actors to bypass endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions. Organizations should implement memory scanning capabilities, monitor COFF loader execution, restrict access to legitimate COFF/BOF runners (such as those in Cobalt Strike), and enforce application whitelisting on development and administrative systems.

The threat actor has progressively increased operational sophistication, shifting from broad targeting to selective focus on corporate environments, with recent payloads utilizing more advanced obfuscation, TLS encryption, and environment-specific reconnaissance scripts. Severity is high given the confirmed ransomware group affiliation, active exploitation, and continuous tool evolution; recommended immediate actions include blocking identified C2 infrastructure, implementing email controls and authentication for Teams/Quick Assist access, training users on vishing tactics, hunting for GoGRPC and related indicators, and deploying behavioral detection for PowerShell-based staging and suspicious process execution patterns.

entry.content:
vulnerability · information-disclosure · CVE-2025-68686

FortiOS is affected by CVE-2025-68686, an exposure of sensitive information vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to bypass previous patches for symbolic link persistence mechanisms through crafted HTTP requests, requiring prior filesystem-level compromise. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild and rated high severity by CISA. Fortinet has released mitigations that must be applied immediately per BOD 26-04 guidance; organizations unable to remediate should discontinue use. All affected systems require forensic triage and evaluation of internet exposure to prioritize patching according to risk assessment protocols.

entry.title: Java Spring Boot "heapdump" scans, (Mon, Jul 27th)
entry.content:
vulnerability · information-disclosure

Spring Boot applications expose the "/actuator/heapdump" endpoint by default, which returns a binary memory dump (heapdump.hprof) containing the application's runtime state including sensitive data such as API keys, database credentials, and other secrets. This is a high-severity information disclosure vulnerability actively exploited in the wild through automated scanning. Organizations should immediately disable the heapdump endpoint in production environments by setting "management.endpoints.web.exposure.exclude=heapdump" in application configuration, or restrict access to actuator endpoints through network controls and authentication mechanisms.

entry.title: OpenAM: WebAuthn Java deserialization RCE via ObjectInputFilter depth>1 bypass (CVE-2026-62263)
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce · CVE-2026-62263

OpenAM's WebAuthn authentication module contains a Java deserialization remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-62263) where an incomplete ObjectInputFilter bypass allows attackers to execute arbitrary code by crafting malicious serialized objects with nested gadget chains. The filter only validates the root object at depth 1, leaving all nested classes unchecked. This is critical severity and requires immediate patching of affected org.openidentityplatform.openam:openam-auth-webauthn versions to implement proper depth-aware deserialization filtering or use a safer serialization mechanism.

entry.title: Budibase: OIDC SSO account takeover: incoming identity linked by email without checking email_verified
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

Budibase's OIDC SSO implementation (npm/@budibase/server) links incoming identities to existing accounts by email address alone without validating the OIDC `email_verified` claim, allowing account takeover. An attacker can create an OIDC identity with an unverified email matching a victim's Budibase account and gain full access to that account with all existing roles preserved. This is critical severity and exploitable in the wild. Upgrade Budibase immediately to a patched version that enforces `email_verified` validation before linking OIDC identities to existing accounts.

entry.title: Budibase: Unauthenticated REST Datasource Credential Theft via Cross-Origin Auth Leak
entry.content:
vulnerability · credential-theft

Budibase npm package prior to patched versions contains a critical vulnerability in REST datasource handling where stored credentials (Bearer tokens, Basic auth, static headers) are attached to outgoing requests before destination validation occurs. An attacker can redirect datasource queries to arbitrary hosts via absolute URLs or parameters, exfiltrating credentials to attacker-controlled servers; exploitation is trivial since queries can be published with PUBLIC role requiring no authentication. This vulnerability is likely being exploited given the ease of weaponization and public disclosure. Immediately update @budibase/server to the patched version and rotate all stored REST datasource credentials; review query configurations for suspicious host redirections.

entry.title: OpenDJ unauthenticated SSRF, local file read and unbounded-read DoS in the DSMLv2 gateway
entry.content:
vulnerability · ssrf

OpenDJ DSML-servlet versions through 5.1.1 contain a critical unauthenticated SSRF vulnerability in the DSMLv2 SOAP gateway that allows attackers to dereference arbitrary URIs without scheme validation or egress filtering. Attackers can exploit this to perform server-side request forgery against internal services and cloud metadata endpoints, read local files via file: URIs, and trigger unbounded-read denial of service attacks. The vulnerability is reachable by default without authentication and affects the opendj-dsml-servlet component. Immediate patching is required; upgrade to a version beyond 5.1.1 if available, or disable the DSMLv2 gateway and implement strict egress filtering and authentication controls as interim mitigation.

entry.title: OpenDJ SASL PLAIN authzid bypassing the proxy ACI scope check
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass

OpenDJ's SASL PLAIN mechanism improperly validates proxy authorization requests by checking only the PROXIED_AUTH privilege while bypassing the mayProxy ACI scope check, allowing any account with proxied-auth privilege to assume any resolvable non-root identity. This vulnerability is critical as it circumvents access control restrictions that are properly enforced by all other proxy paths in OpenDJ. The issue affects org.openidentityplatform.opendj:opendj-server-legacy and should be patched immediately by upgrading to a patched version that validates both PROXIED_AUTH privilege and mayProxy ACI checks for SASL PLAIN authzid resolution.
